biography.plain_text: Robert L. Hixson Jr. is an American lumber executive and former head of Hixson Lumber Sales. He guided a family enterprise that supplied pressure-treated wood, fencing and other building materials through a broad central US network. Beyond the timber trade, Hixson spent almost twenty years transforming a South Texas property into a commercial hunting operation.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Hixson Lumber Sales, Robert L. Hixson Jr. held both ownership and executive responsibility. The enterprise linked wholesale distribution to wood preservation, fence production, specialist mills and an in-house transport fleet. By the time Doman Building Materials purchased the business, it employed roughly 1,100 people and ran facilities in eight states.

Hixson also pursued a separate land-based venture. After buying La Bandera Ranch in 2001, he managed it for paying hunting guests and improved its habitat, access roads and water supply. Lodges, a paved runway and a large hangar supported the operation. The ranch changed hands after nearly two decades; the lumber company followed in 2021, when Doman folded it into a wider North American building-materials platform.
